sourceName: JRC GHSL GHS-POP R2023A（2020年人口推計）
attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (JRC), GHS-POP R2023A; Canada aggregation and cartography by Insight Journal.

source.dataNature: Published spatial population model informed by census/administrative estimates and built-up information; not direct household observations
source.valueUnit: estimated persons per original 1 km² equal-area cell
source.citation: Schiavina, Freire, Carioli and MacManus, GHS-POP R2023A, European Commission Joint Research Centre

processing.aggregation: Aligned 5×5 original 1 km Mollweide cells: sum source population in float64 / count of valid original 1 km² cells; -200/nonfinite excluded from both; all-missing blocks stay -1; valid zeros remain zero. Convert aggregate once to Float32.
processing.display: Each Canada-masked Web Mercator output pixel centre selects the containing aligned 5 km source block (nearest aggregate). No continuous interpolation, national averages or independent population allocation.
processing.mask: Existing Canada country outline, even-odd polygon/hole inclusion at output pixel centres; outside pixels transparent and -1. No coastline expansion or nearest-land fill.
processing.boundarySource: Natural Earth public domain; existing site country geometry
processing.pngGridEquality: Every lossless PNG pixel classifies the same Float32 sample stored in the lossless gzip lookup; both exact roundtrips checked.

limitations: 2020 modelled source population distribution; not 2021 Census counts or a 2026 population measure.
The original source is 1 km, the chosen aggregate is 5 km; approximately 9.9 km Web Mercator display pixels do not increase detail, and their ground scale varies by latitude.
Density denominator is valid equal-area source cells, including valid zero/water cells, not administrative land area. Aggregated border cells can cross water or neighbouring territory.

The destination Canada outline masks surrounding countries but is generalized; small islands/coasts or concentrations between display pixel centres may be omitted. No invented population is added to gaps.
A CMA display-anchor pixel is a local modelled density sample, not that city's/CMA's population or mean density.
Do not sum display pixels or densities to infer Canada, provincial, municipal or urban-centre population totals.
